7. HIPAA Safe-Harbour De-identification

# HIPAA Safe Harbour requires removal of 18 identifiers before data sharing.
# This function demonstrates the safe-harbour checks on a data frame.

HIPAA_IDENTIFIERS <- c(
  "name", "geographic_data_smaller_than_state", "dates_except_year",
  "phone", "fax", "email", "ssn", "mrn", "health_plan_id",
  "account_number", "certificate_license", "vehicle_id", "device_id",
  "url", "ip_address", "biometric", "full_face_photo", "any_unique_id"
)

# Simulate a raw dataset with some PHI columns
df_raw <- df_pts
df_raw$full_name <- paste("Patient", seq_len(nrow(df_raw)) - 1)
df_raw$phone     <- paste0("555-", sample(1000000:9999999, nrow(df_raw), replace = TRUE))
df_raw$email     <- paste0("pt", seq_len(nrow(df_raw)) - 1, "@example.com")
df_raw$ssn_last4 <- as.character(sample(1000:9999, nrow(df_raw), replace = TRUE))

safe_harbour_check <- function(df) {
  # Flag columns that may contain PHI based on name heuristics.
  phi_keywords <- c("name", "phone", "fax", "email", "ssn", "mrn", "dob", "birth",
                    "address", "zip", "ip", "device", "url", "id_", "npi")
  flagged <- character()
  for (col in names(df)) {
    if (any(vapply(phi_keywords, function(kw) grepl(kw, tolower(col), fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))) {
      flagged <- c(flagged, col)
    }
  }
  flagged
}

flagged_cols <- safe_harbour_check(df_raw)
cat("Columns flagged as potential PHI:\n")

Columns flagged as potential PHI:

for (col in flagged_cols) cat(sprintf("  ⚠  %s\n", col))

  ⚠  birthDate
  ⚠  zip
  ⚠  full_name
  ⚠  phone
  ⚠  email
  ⚠  ssn_last4

# De-identify: drop PHI, generalise ZIP to 3-digit
deidentify <- function(df, phi_cols, zip_col = NULL) {
  keep <- setdiff(names(df), intersect(phi_cols, names(df)))
  df_clean <- df[keep]
  if (!is.null(zip_col) && zip_col %in% names(df_clean)) {
    # HIPAA: 3-digit ZIP if population > 20,000; else replace with 000
    df_clean[[zip_col]] <- paste0(substr(df_clean[[zip_col]], 1, 3), "XX")
  }
  df_clean
}

8. Code Quality Validation Pipeline

# Build a reusable validation function that checks ICD, CPT, and LOINC
# codes in a data frame and produces a quality report.

validate_code_column <- function(series, code_type) {
  # Validate a column of clinical codes. code_type: 'icd10', 'cpt', or 'loinc'
  purrr::map_dfr(series, function(code) {
    if (is.na(code) || identical(code, "")) {
      return(tibble(code = as.character(code), valid = FALSE, reason = "Missing/empty"))
    }
    code <- trimws(as.character(code))
    if (code_type == "icd10") {
      r <- parse_icd10cm(code)
      tibble(code = code, valid = isTRUE(r$valid),
             reason = if (isTRUE(r$valid)) "" else "Invalid ICD-10 format")
    } else if (code_type == "cpt") {
      r <- validate_cpt(code)
      tibble(code = code, valid = isTRUE(r$valid), reason = r$notes)
    } else if (code_type == "loinc") {
      valid <- grepl("^[0-9]{2,5}-[0-9]$", code)
      tibble(code = code, valid = valid,
             reason = if (valid) "" else "Invalid LOINC format (expected NNNNN-C)")
    } else {
      tibble(code = code, valid = FALSE, reason = "Unknown code_type")
    }
  })
}

# --- Test with mixed valid/invalid codes ---
test_icd   <- c("E11.9", "I10", "BADCODE", "", "Z87.891", "XYZ")
test_cpt   <- c("99213", "27447", "1234", "ABCDE", "71046")
test_loinc <- c("2345-7", "718-7", "99999", "loinc_bad", "4548-4")

for (item in list(
  list(name = "ICD-10", series = test_icd,   ctype = "icd10"),
  list(name = "CPT",    series = test_cpt,   ctype = "cpt"),
  list(name = "LOINC",  series = test_loinc, ctype = "loinc")
)) {
  result    <- validate_code_column(item$series, item$ctype)
  valid_pct <- mean(result$valid) * 100
  cat(sprintf("%s — valid: %.0f%%\n", item$name, valid_pct))
  print(result)
  cat("\n")
}

Health data pipelines use four foundational R structures. Understanding them prevents the most common data-wrangling errors.

3. Synthetic Health Dataset
We generate a realistic synthetic hospital discharge dataset so every learner starts from the same data without any data-use-agreement requirements.
In real projects this would be replaced by a CMS, HCUP NIS, or EHR export.

set.seed(42)
N <- 500

# --- Controlled random draws to mimic real discharge distributions ---
ages  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, mean = 62, sd = 16), 18), 95))
sexes <- sample(c("M", "F"), size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
  size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03)
)
drg_codes <- sample(c(470, 291, 392, 690, 871, 193, 247, 603), size = N, replace = TRUE)
drg_labels_map <- c(
  `470` = "Major joint replacement", `291` = "Heart failure & shock",
  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges  <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
missing_mask <- runif(N) < 0.08   # 8% missing charges (realistic)
charges[missing_mask] <- NA_real_

primary_dx <- sample(
  c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "I50.9", "J18.9", "A41.9", "M16.11", "N39.0"),
  size = N, replace = TRUE
)
admit_type <- sample(
  c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
  size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02)
)

df <- tibble(
  patient_id   = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age          = ages,
  sex          = sexes,
  payer        = payers,
  drg_code     = drg_codes,
  drg_label    = unname(drg_labels_map[as.character(drg_codes)]),
  primary_dx   = primary_dx,
  admit_type   = admit_type,
  los_days     = los_days,
  total_charge = charges
)

7. ICD-10 & DRG Code Structures

# ICD-10-CM structure: Category . Etiology/Anatomic site . Severity
parse_icd10 <- function(code) {
  code <- gsub("\\.", "", code)
  category <- substr(code, 1, 3)
  if (nchar(code) > 3) {
    subcategory <- substr(code, 4, 4)
    detail      <- if (nchar(code) > 4) substr(code, 5, nchar(code)) else ""
  } else {
    subcategory <- ""
    detail      <- ""
  }
  list(category = category, subcategory = subcategory, detail = detail)
}

for (icd in c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "A41.9")) {
  parsed <- parse_icd10(icd)
  cat(sprintf("  %-8s → category=%s  subcategory=%s  detail=%s\n",
              icd, parsed$category, parsed$subcategory, parsed$detail))
}

  I10      → category=I10  subcategory=  detail=
  N18.3    → category=N18  subcategory=3  detail=
  A41.9    → category=A41  subcategory=9  detail=

Why Health Analytics with R?
Healthcare generates more data per person than almost any other industry — electronic health records, claims databases, imaging, genomics, wearables, and administrative files — yet much of it remains under-analysed. This series bridges three gaps that most textbooks leave open:

Clinically meaningful examples — every dataset, model, and metric is grounded in real healthcare problems: readmission prediction, drug optimisation, spatial health inequities, and causal treatment effects.
End-to-end thinking — notebooks do not stop at model accuracy. They continue through calibration, fairness, explainability, API serving, monitoring, and clinical governance.
Reproducibility by design — code is written as it would be in a health system data science team: version-pinned environments, SHA-256 data manifests, logged pipelines, and CI/CD-ready test suites.

A Comprehensive Tutorial Series


🏥 Health Analytics with R


From Raw EHR Data to Production-Ready Clinical Models





Modules


8 modules · 62 notebooks · ~450 code cells




Level


Intermediate to Advanced · Healthcare data science background assumed




Language


R 4.3+ · Quarto-compatible




Dataset


Synthetic (MIMIC-III inspired) · seed = 42 throughout




Author


Dr. Zia U. Ahmed · Upatta Analytics · zia207 @ GitHub






1. Why Health Analytics with R?
Healthcare generates more data per person than almost any other industry — electronic health records, claims databases, imaging, genomics, wearables, and administrative files — yet much of it remains under-analysed. R has become the language of choice for many epidemiologists and health data scientists because of its rich ecosystem spanning statistics, machine learning, natural language processing, geospatial analysis, and production deployment.
This series bridges three gaps that most textbooks leave open:

Clinically meaningful examples — every dataset, model, and metric is grounded in real healthcare problems: readmission prediction, drug optimisation, spatial health inequities, causal effects of treatment.
End-to-end thinking — notebooks do not stop at model accuracy. They continue through calibration, fairness, explainability, API serving, monitoring, and clinical governance.
Reproducibility by design — code is written as it would be in a health system data science team: version-pinned environments, SHA-256 data manifests, logged pipelines, and CI/CD-ready test suites.


Who is this for? Health informatics professionals, clinical data scientists, epidemiologists, public health researchers, and graduate students who know R basics and want to apply it rigorously to healthcare problems.

check_pkg <- function(name, min_ver) {
  if (requireNamespace(name, quietly = TRUE)) {
    ver <- as.character(utils::packageVersion(name))
    ok  <- utils::compareVersion(ver, min_ver) >= 0
    list(ver = ver, status = if (ok) "OK" else "UPGRADE")
  } else {
    list(ver = "not installed", status = "MISSING")
  }
}

Preview: A Taste of Every Module

# ── Quick-start: a taste of what each module delivers ──────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 1800

sigmoid <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

# ── Shared synthetic cohort ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
age  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 63, 14), 18), 90))
los  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 28))
hf   <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.22)
dm   <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.35)
copd <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.18)
payer <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.10)
)
logit   <- -3.2 + 0.6 * hf + 0.5 * dm + 0.3 * copd + 0.02 * (age - 63) + 0.2 * (los > 7)
readmit <- rbinom(N, 1, sigmoid(logit))
cvd_rate <- 180 + 1.4 * rnorm(N, 10, 5) + 12 * rnorm(N, 0, 1)

df <- tibble(
  age      = age,
  los      = los,
  hf       = hf,
  dm       = dm,
  copd     = copd,
  payer    = payer,
  readmit  = readmit,
  cvd_rate = cvd_rate
)

cat(sprintf("Cohort: N=%s | Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n",
            format(N, big.mark = ","), mean(readmit) * 100))

Cohort: N=1,800 | Readmission rate: 6.1%

cat("Building preview figure ...\n")

Building preview figure ...



# ── 8-panel preview figure — one panel per module ───────────────────────────
BLUE   <- "#2563EB"; RED    <- "#DC2626"; GREEN  <- "#16A34A"
GOLD   <- "#D97706"; PURPLE <- "#7C3AED"; TEAL   <- "#0D9488"
GRAY   <- "#6B7280"; PINK   <- "#DB2777"

theme_preview <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, lineheight = 1.1)
    )
}

# Stratified 80/20 split (matches tidymodels/rsample strata, seed = 42)
set.seed(42)
df <- df %>% mutate(.row = dplyr::row_number())
train <- df %>%
  group_by(readmit) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 0.8) %>%
  ungroup()
test <- dplyr::anti_join(df, train, by = ".row")

n_tr <- nrow(train)
n1   <- sum(train$readmit == 1)
n0   <- n_tr - n1
train$w <- ifelse(train$readmit == 1, n_tr / (2 * n1), n_tr / (2 * n0))

model <- glm(
  readmit ~ age + los + hf + dm + copd,
  family  = quasibinomial(),
  data    = train,
  weights = w
)
prob <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = test, type = "response"))
y_te <- test$readmit

roc_curve_df <- function(y, p) {
  y <- as.integer(y)
  o <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE)
  y <- y[o]
  tp <- cumsum(y)
  fp <- cumsum(1L - y)
  tibble(
    fpr = c(0, fp / max(fp[length(fp)], 1), 1),
    tpr = c(0, tp / max(tp[length(tp)], 1), 1)
  )
}
auc_trap <- function(fpr, tpr) {
  o   <- order(fpr)
  fpr <- fpr[o]
  tpr <- tpr[o]
  sum(diff(fpr) * (utils::head(tpr, -1) + utils::tail(tpr, -1)) / 2)
}
roc_df <- roc_curve_df(y_te, prob)
auc    <- auc_trap(roc_df$fpr, roc_df$tpr)

# ── Panel 1: MOD-02 · EDA — readmission by payer ─────────────────────────────
overall_rate <- mean(df$readmit) * 100
payer_r <- df %>%
  group_by(payer) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(readmit) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(rate)) %>%
  mutate(
    payer = factor(payer, levels = payer),
    fill  = ifelse(rate > overall_rate + 2, RED, BLUE)
  )

p1 <- ggplot(payer_r, aes(payer, rate, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = overall_rate, colour = GRAY, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", rate)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(
    y = "30-day readmission rate (%)",
    x = NULL,
    title = "MOD-02 · EDA\nReadmission Rate by Payer"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 18, hjust = 1, size = 8))

# ── Panel 2: MOD-03 · Statistics — survival curve ─────────────────────────────
t_max <- 30
times <- seq(0, t_max, length.out = 200)
surv_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    days  = times,
    surv  = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 1], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)),
    group = "Heart Failure"
  ),
  tibble(
    days  = times,
    surv  = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 0], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)),
    group = "No HF"
  )
)

p2 <- ggplot(surv_df, aes(days, surv, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = surv), alpha = 0.08, colour = NA) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days", y = "Survival (in-hospital)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "MOD-03 · Statistics\nKaplan-Meier by HF Status"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.88), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# ── Panel 3: MOD-04 · ML — ROC curve ─────────────────────────────────────────
p3 <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), fill = RED, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_line(colour = RED, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = 0.18, label = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc),
           colour = RED, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    x = "1 − Specificity", y = "Sensitivity",
    title = "MOD-04 · Machine Learning\nROC Curve — Readmission Model"
  ) +
  theme_preview()

# ── Panel 4: MOD-05 · NLP — entity frequency bar ─────────────────────────────
entities <- c("MEDICATION", "DIAGNOSIS", "PROCEDURE", "LAB_VALUE",
              "VITAL_SIGN", "DATE", "PROVIDER")
counts <- c(340, 285, 198, 423, 312, 510, 87) + sample(-15:15, 7, replace = TRUE)
ner_df <- tibble(
  entity = factor(entities, levels = rev(entities)),
  count  = counts,
  fill   = c(BLUE, RED, GREEN, GOLD, PURPLE, TEAL, PINK)
)

p4 <- ggplot(ner_df, aes(count, entity, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(ner_df$count) * 1.12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Entity count (synthetic discharge notes)", y = NULL,
    title = "MOD-05 · Clinical NLP\nclinicalBERT Named Entity Recognition"
  ) +
  theme_preview()

# ── Panel 5: MOD-06 · Causal — Love plot (balance) ───────────────────────────
love_df <- tibble(
  covariate = factor(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"),
                     levels = rev(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"))),
  Unadjusted      = c(0.38, 0.27, 0.45, 0.31, 0.22),
  `IPTW weighted` = c(0.04, 0.03, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-covariate, names_to = "method", values_to = "smd")

p5 <- ggplot(love_df, aes(smd, covariate, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.32, colour = "white", alpha = 0.80) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Unadjusted" = RED, "IPTW weighted" = BLUE)) +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute SMD", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "MOD-06 · Causal Inference\nLove Plot — IPTW Balance"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.22), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# ── Panel 6: MOD-07 · Geospatial — synthetic scatter map ─────────────────────
set.seed(7)
N_c <- 200
geo <- tibble(
  lon = runif(N_c, -120, -70),
  lat = runif(N_c, 28, 48)
) %>%
  mutate(cvd = 180 + 1.4 * (lon + 95) + 12 * rnorm(N_c, 0, 1))
tt   <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 120)
circ <- tibble(x = -100 + 8 * cos(tt), y = 33 + 8 * sin(tt))

p6 <- ggplot(geo, aes(lon, lat, colour = cvd)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.80) +
  geom_path(data = circ, aes(x, y), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed",
            linewidth = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = -100, y = 24.5, label = "Hot spot\n(scan stat)",
           size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#1A9850", "#FDE725", "#D73027"),
                         name = "CVD rate/100k") +
  labs(
    x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude",
    title = "MOD-07 · Spatial Epi\nCVD Mortality + Cluster Detection"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5))

# ── Panel 7: MOD-08 · Deployment — drift monitoring ──────────────────────────
quarters <- c("23-Q1", "23-Q2", "23-Q3", "23-Q4", "24-Q1", "24-Q2")
drift <- tibble(
  quarter    = factor(quarters, levels = quarters),
  Overall    = c(0.789, 0.784, 0.780, 0.771, 0.758, 0.745),
  `Black/AA` = c(0.775, 0.769, 0.764, 0.751, 0.735, 0.718)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-quarter, names_to = "group", values_to = "auc")

p7 <- ggplot(drift, aes(quarter, auc, colour = group, group = group)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf,
           ymin = 0.789 - 0.05, ymax = 0.789 - 0.03,
           fill = "orange", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.789 - 0.03, colour = "orange", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.789 - 0.05, colour = RED,      linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = group), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Overall" = BLUE, "Black/AA" = RED)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Overall" = "solid", "Black/AA" = "dashed")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.68, 0.82)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "AUC-ROC", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "MOD-08 · Deployment\nModel Drift & Fairness Monitoring"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.28, 0.22), legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))

# ── Panel 8: Series overview donut ───────────────────────────────────────────
donut <- tibble(
  label = c("Foundations\n& EDA", "Statistics\n& Survival", "Machine\nLearning",
            "Clinical NLP", "Causal\nInference", "Spatial Epi", "Deployment\n& MLOps"),
  n     = 8,
  fill  = c(TEAL, BLUE, RED, GREEN, GOLD, PURPLE, GRAY)
) %>%
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label))

p8 <- ggplot(donut, aes(x = 2, y = n, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 2.75, label = label),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.4, lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0, label = "62",
           size = 8, fontface = "bold", colour = "#1F2937") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0, label = "\n\nnotebooks",
           size = 3.1, colour = GRAY) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = pi / 2) +
  xlim(0.5, 3.3) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(title = "HealthR Series\nModule Distribution") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 1.1)
  )

preview <- (p1 | p2 | p3 | p4) / (p5 | p6 | p7 | p8) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Health Analytics with R  ·  Series Preview",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
    )

4. How to Use This Series

Option A — RStudio / Posit Cloud (Recommended for beginners)
Open any .qmd file in RStudio or Posit Cloud. Quarto renders HTML with a table of contents; Posit Cloud provides a free hosted R session.

source("packages.R")


Option B — Local Quarto / RStudio

git clone https://github.com/zia207/Health-Analytics-with-Python.git
cd Health-Analytics-with-Python/Health-Analytics-R

# 2. Install all dependencies

# 3. Open the project in RStudio, or render from the command line
quarto preview


Option C — VS Code + Quarto Extension
Open any .qmd file directly in VS Code with the Quarto extension. Select the R kernel created above.



Running Order
New to health data science?    → MOD-01 → MOD-02 → MOD-03 → MOD-04
Want ML for clinical prediction? → MOD-04 (then MOD-05 for NLP, MOD-08 for deployment)
Interested in causal inference?  → MOD-06 (requires MOD-03 background)
Spatial epidemiology focus?      → MOD-07 (requires MOD-02 EDA)
Building a production pipeline?  → MOD-08 (works standalone)



5. Series Conventions
Reproducibility first - All notebooks use set.seed(42) as the first executable cell - Synthetic datasets are generated in-memory; no downloads required - A shared helper pattern regenerates the same cohort across all notebooks in a module
Code style - tidyverse style, snake_case, max line length 100 characters - Documented function signatures with argument descriptions - Comments on every function: purpose, args, returns - Tested with testthat; CI via GitHub Actions
Figures - All publication figures saved at 300 dpi via ggsave(..., dpi = 300) - Consistent colour palette: #2563EB (blue) / #DC2626 (red) / #16A34A (green) - Colourblind-accessible palettes used throughout
Dataset conventions | Symbol | Meaning | |——–|———| | N | sample size | | df | primary working data frame / tibble | | X_tr, X_te | train / test feature matrices | | y_tr, y_te | train / test target vectors | | FEATURES | list of predictor column names | | TRUE_EFFECT | known simulation parameter (for validation) |
Notebook structure (every NB follows this pattern) 1. Title, learning objectives, estimated time 2. ## 1. Setup — imports, dataset generation, seed 3. ## 2–N — core content sections 4. Knowledge Check — 5 questions 5. Exercises — at least one executable cell per exercise 6. ---  Next → NB-0X — explicit navigation footer


6. Datasets & Data Ethics

Synthetic data — why not real patient data?
All notebooks use synthetic data generated with controlled random seeds. This approach:

Allows open publication without IRB restrictions or HIPAA concerns
Lets us embed known ground-truth effects so learners can verify their results
Reproduces identical results across operating systems and time

The synthetic data are designed to mimic the statistical properties of real EHR data (MIMIC-III), with realistic covariate distributions, correlation structures, and outcome rates.


Data Ethics Principles Embedded in This Series







Module
Embedded ethics topic




MOD-04
Calibration and algorithmic fairness across demographic groups


MOD-05
De-identification of PHI before NLP model training


MOD-06
Causal assumptions and the limits of observational data


MOD-07
Environmental justice and spatial health disparities


MOD-08
Model Cards, governance checklists, patient-facing explanations




A note on race in clinical models: Where race/ethnicity appears in the synthetic data, it is used to audit fairness — never as a predictor variable. The series explicitly demonstrates how models can encode proxy-bias even when race is excluded from features.

title: Health Analytics with R
text:
1. Why Health Analytics with R?
Healthcare generates more data per person than almost any other industry — electronic health records, claims databases, imaging, genomics, wearables, and administrative files — yet much of it remains under-analysed. R has become the language of choice for many epidemiologists and health data scientists because of its rich ecosystem spanning statistics, machine learning, natural language processing, geospatial analysis, and production deployment.
This series bridges three gaps that most textbooks leave open:

Clinically meaningful examples — every dataset, model, and metric is grounded in real healthcare problems: readmission prediction, drug optimisation, spatial health inequities, causal effects of treatment.
End-to-end thinking — notebooks do not stop at model accuracy. They continue through calibration, fairness, explainability, API serving, monitoring, and clinical governance.
Reproducibility by design — code is written as it would be in a health system data science team: version-pinned environments, SHA-256 data manifests, logged pipelines, and CI/CD-ready test suites.


Who is this for? Health informatics professionals, clinical data scientists, epidemiologists, public health researchers, and graduate students who know R basics and want to apply it rigorously to healthcare problems.

Preview: A Taste of Every Module

# ── Quick-start: a taste of what each module delivers ──────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 1800

sigmoid <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

# ── Shared synthetic cohort ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
age  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 63, 14), 18), 90))
los  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 28))
hf   <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.22)
dm   <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.35)
copd <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.18)
payer <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.10)
)
logit   <- -3.2 + 0.6 * hf + 0.5 * dm + 0.3 * copd + 0.02 * (age - 63) + 0.2 * (los > 7)
readmit <- rbinom(N, 1, sigmoid(logit))
cvd_rate <- 180 + 1.4 * rnorm(N, 10, 5) + 12 * rnorm(N, 0, 1)

df <- tibble(
  age      = age,
  los      = los,
  hf       = hf,
  dm       = dm,
  copd     = copd,
  payer    = payer,
  readmit  = readmit,
  cvd_rate = cvd_rate
)

cat(sprintf("Cohort: N=%s | Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n",
            format(N, big.mark = ","), mean(readmit) * 100))

Cohort: N=1,800 | Readmission rate: 6.1%

cat("Building preview figure ...\n")

Building preview figure ...



# ── 8-panel preview figure — one panel per module ───────────────────────────
BLUE   <- "#2563EB"; RED    <- "#DC2626"; GREEN  <- "#16A34A"
GOLD   <- "#D97706"; PURPLE <- "#7C3AED"; TEAL   <- "#0D9488"
GRAY   <- "#6B7280"; PINK   <- "#DB2777"

theme_preview <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, lineheight = 1.1)
    )
}

# Stratified 80/20 split (matches tidymodels/rsample strata, seed = 42)
set.seed(42)
df <- df %>% mutate(.row = dplyr::row_number())
train <- df %>%
  group_by(readmit) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 0.8) %>%
  ungroup()
test <- dplyr::anti_join(df, train, by = ".row")

n_tr <- nrow(train)
n1   <- sum(train$readmit == 1)
n0   <- n_tr - n1
train$w <- ifelse(train$readmit == 1, n_tr / (2 * n1), n_tr / (2 * n0))

model <- glm(
  readmit ~ age + los + hf + dm + copd,
  family  = quasibinomial(),
  data    = train,
  weights = w
)
prob <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = test, type = "response"))
y_te <- test$readmit

roc_curve_df <- function(y, p) {
  y <- as.integer(y)
  o <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE)
  y <- y[o]
  tp <- cumsum(y)
  fp <- cumsum(1L - y)
  tibble(
    fpr = c(0, fp / max(fp[length(fp)], 1), 1),
    tpr = c(0, tp / max(tp[length(tp)], 1), 1)
  )
}
auc_trap <- function(fpr, tpr) {
  o   <- order(fpr)
  fpr <- fpr[o]
  tpr <- tpr[o]
  sum(diff(fpr) * (utils::head(tpr, -1) + utils::tail(tpr, -1)) / 2)
}
roc_df <- roc_curve_df(y_te, prob)
auc    <- auc_trap(roc_df$fpr, roc_df$tpr)

# ── Panel 1: MOD-02 · EDA — readmission by payer ─────────────────────────────
overall_rate <- mean(df$readmit) * 100
payer_r <- df %>%
  group_by(payer) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(readmit) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(rate)) %>%
  mutate(
    payer = factor(payer, levels = payer),
    fill  = ifelse(rate > overall_rate + 2, RED, BLUE)
  )

p1 <- ggplot(payer_r, aes(payer, rate, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = overall_rate, colour = GRAY, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", rate)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(
    y = "30-day readmission rate (%)",
    x = NULL,
    title = "MOD-02 · EDA\nReadmission Rate by Payer"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 18, hjust = 1, size = 8))

# ── Panel 2: MOD-03 · Statistics — survival curve ─────────────────────────────
t_max <- 30
times <- seq(0, t_max, length.out = 200)
surv_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    days  = times,
    surv  = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 1], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)),
    group = "Heart Failure"
  ),
  tibble(
    days  = times,
    surv  = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 0], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)),
    group = "No HF"
  )
)

p2 <- ggplot(surv_df, aes(days, surv, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = surv), alpha = 0.08, colour = NA) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days", y = "Survival (in-hospital)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "MOD-03 · Statistics\nKaplan-Meier by HF Status"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.88), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# ── Panel 3: MOD-04 · ML — ROC curve ─────────────────────────────────────────
p3 <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), fill = RED, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_line(colour = RED, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = 0.18, label = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc),
           colour = RED, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    x = "1 − Specificity", y = "Sensitivity",
    title = "MOD-04 · Machine Learning\nROC Curve — Readmission Model"
  ) +
  theme_preview()

# ── Panel 4: MOD-05 · NLP — entity frequency bar ─────────────────────────────
entities <- c("MEDICATION", "DIAGNOSIS", "PROCEDURE", "LAB_VALUE",
              "VITAL_SIGN", "DATE", "PROVIDER")
counts <- c(340, 285, 198, 423, 312, 510, 87) + sample(-15:15, 7, replace = TRUE)
ner_df <- tibble(
  entity = factor(entities, levels = rev(entities)),
  count  = counts,
  fill   = c(BLUE, RED, GREEN, GOLD, PURPLE, TEAL, PINK)
)

p4 <- ggplot(ner_df, aes(count, entity, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(ner_df$count) * 1.12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Entity count (synthetic discharge notes)", y = NULL,
    title = "MOD-05 · Clinical NLP\nclinicalBERT Named Entity Recognition"
  ) +
  theme_preview()

# ── Panel 5: MOD-06 · Causal — Love plot (balance) ───────────────────────────
love_df <- tibble(
  covariate = factor(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"),
                     levels = rev(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"))),
  Unadjusted      = c(0.38, 0.27, 0.45, 0.31, 0.22),
  `IPTW weighted` = c(0.04, 0.03, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-covariate, names_to = "method", values_to = "smd")

p5 <- ggplot(love_df, aes(smd, covariate, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.32, colour = "white", alpha = 0.80) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Unadjusted" = RED, "IPTW weighted" = BLUE)) +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute SMD", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "MOD-06 · Causal Inference\nLove Plot — IPTW Balance"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.22), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# ── Panel 6: MOD-07 · Geospatial — synthetic scatter map ─────────────────────
set.seed(7)
N_c <- 200
geo <- tibble(
  lon = runif(N_c, -120, -70),
  lat = runif(N_c, 28, 48)
) %>%

5. Series Conventions
Reproducibility first - All notebooks use set.seed(42) as the first executable cell - Synthetic datasets are generated in-memory; no downloads required - A shared helper pattern regenerates the same cohort across all notebooks in a module
Code style - tidyverse style, snake_case, max line length 100 characters - Documented function signatures with argument descriptions - Comments on every function: purpose, args, returns - Tested with testthat; CI via GitHub Actions
Figures - All publication figures saved at 300 dpi via ggsave(..., dpi = 300) - Consistent colour palette: #2563EB (blue) / #DC2626 (red) / #16A34A (green) - Colourblind-accessible palettes used throughout

Notebook structure (every NB follows this pattern) 1. Title, learning objectives, estimated time 2. ## 1. Setup — imports, dataset generation, seed 3. ## 2–N — core content sections 4. title: Health Analytics with R
text:
6. Datasets & Data Ethics

Synthetic data — why not real patient data?
All notebooks use synthetic data generated with controlled random seeds. This approach:

Allows open publication without IRB restrictions or HIPAA concerns
Lets us embed known ground-truth effects so learners can verify their results
Reproduces identical results across operating systems and time

The synthetic data are designed to mimic the statistical properties of real EHR data (MIMIC-III), with realistic covariate distributions, correlation structures, and outcome rates.


Data Ethics Principles Embedded in This Series







Module
Embedded ethics topic




MOD-04
Calibration and algorithmic fairness across demographic groups


MOD-05
De-identification of PHI before NLP model training


MOD-06
Causal assumptions and the limits of observational data


MOD-07
Environmental justice and spatial health disparities


MOD-08
Model Cards, governance checklists, patient-facing explanations




A note on race in clinical models: Where race/ethnicity appears in the synthetic data, it is used to audit fairness — never as a predictor variable. The series explicitly demonstrates how models can encode proxy-bias even when race is excluded from features.

library(tidyverse)

# Rebuild the same synthetic dataset from NB-01 (identical seed)

  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)

# Add comorbidities
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),

Readmission rate    : 13.8 per 100 discharges



# --- 2.3  95% confidence interval for a proportion (Wilson method) ---
wilson_ci <- function(k, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  # Wilson score interval — preferred for proportions near 0 or 1.
  z         <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  p_hat     <- k / n
  denom     <- 1 + z^2 / n
  centre    <- (p_hat + z^2 / (2 * n)) / denom
  half_width <- (z * sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))) / denom
  c(
    lo = round((centre - half_width) * 100, 1),
    hi = round((centre + half_width) * 100, 1)
  )
}

ci <- wilson_ci(readmissions, total_discharges)
cat(sprintf("Readmission rate: %.1f%% (95%% CI: %s%% – %s%%)\n",
            rate_per_100, ci["lo"], ci["hi"]))

4. Interpreting Skewed Clinical Distributions

# --- 4.1  LOS skewness and kurtosis ---
skewness <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  mean((x - m)^3) / (s^3)
}
kurtosis_ex <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  mean((x - m)^4) / (s^4) - 3
}

los <- df$los_days[!is.na(df$los_days)]
chg <- df$total_charge[!is.na(df$total_charge)]

for (pair in list(list("LOS (days)", los), list("Total charge ($)", chg))) {
  name   <- pair[[1]]
  series <- pair[[2]]
  sk     <- skewness(series)
  cat(name, "\n", sep = "")
  cat(sprintf("  Mean   : %.2f\n", mean(series)))
  cat(sprintf("  Median : %.2f\n", median(series)))
  cat(sprintf("  Std    : %.2f\n", sd(series)))
  cat(sprintf("  Skew   : %.3f  %s\n", sk,
              if (sk > 0.5) "(right-skewed — median is preferred)" else ""))
  cat(sprintf("  Kurtosis: %.3f\n\n", kurtosis_ex(series)))
}

text:
5. Age-Standardisation (Direct Method)

# Direct age-standardisation: applies study rates to a standard population
# to remove confounding by age structure differences between groups.

# US 2000 Standard Population weights by age group
std_pop <- tibble(
  age_group  = factor(c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"),
                      levels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+")),
  std_weight = c(0.3761, 0.3399, 0.1267, 0.0573)   # proportions sum to ~1
)

# Crude rates by age group × payer (Medicare vs Private as example)
for (pay in c("Medicare", "Private")) {
  sub <- df %>% filter(payer == pay)
  rates <- sub %>%
    group_by(age_group) %>%
    summarise(
      crude_rate = mean(readmitted_30),
      n          = n(),
      .groups    = "drop"
    ) %>%
    left_join(std_pop, by = "age_group") %>%
    mutate(weighted_rate = crude_rate * std_weight)
  age_adj_rate  <- sum(rates$weighted_rate, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  crude_overall <- mean(sub$readmitted_30) * 100
  cat(sprintf("%-10s — Crude: %.1f%%  |  Age-adjusted: %.1f%%\n",
              pay, crude_overall, age_adj_rate))
}

Medicare   — Crude: 15.4%  |  Age-adjusted: 11.8%
Private    — Crude: 9.0%  |  Age-adjusted: 8.8%

title: Descriptive Statistics & Health Metrics
text:
6. Table 1 — Publication-Ready Descriptive Table
A “Table 1” in clinical research summarises the baseline characteristics of a cohort, often stratified by a key variable (e.g. readmitted vs not).

table1 <- function(df, stratify_col, continuous_cols, categorical_cols) {
  # Build a basic Table 1.
  # Continuous: mean ± SD (or median [IQR] if skewed)
  # Categorical: N (%)
  groups <- sort(unique(df[[stratify_col]]))
  group_label <- function(g) {
    n <- sum(df[[stratify_col]] == g, na.rm = TRUE)
    pretty <- if (identical(g, 0) || identical(g, 0L)) {
      "Not readmitted"
    } else if (identical(g, 1) || identical(g, 1L)) {
      "Readmitted"
    } else {
      as.character(g)
    }
    sprintf("%s (N=%d)", pretty, n)
  }

  rows <- list()
  header <- c(Variable = "Variable")
  for (g in groups) header[[as.character(g)]] <- group_label(g)
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- header

  for (col in continuous_cols) {
    sk  <- abs(skewness(df[[col]]))
    row <- c(Variable = paste0(col, if (sk > 1) " [median, IQR]" else " [mean ± SD]"))
    for (g in groups) {
      vals <- df[[col]][df[[stratify_col]] == g]
      vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
      row[[as.character(g)]] <- if (sk > 1) {
        sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", median(vals), quantile(vals, 0.25), quantile(vals, 0.75))
      } else {
        sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f", mean(vals), sd(vals))
      }
    }
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- row
  }

  for (col in categorical_cols) {
    row <- c(Variable = col)
    for (g in groups) row[[as.character(g)]] <- ""
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- row
    cats <- unique(df[[col]][!is.na(df[[col]])])
    for (cat in cats) {
      row <- c(Variable = paste0("  ", as.character(cat)))
      for (g in groups) {
        sub   <- df[df[[stratify_col]] == g, ]
        n_cat <- sum(sub[[col]] == cat, na.rm = TRUE)
        pct   <- n_cat / nrow(sub) * 100
        row[[as.character(g)]] <- sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_cat, pct)
      }
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- row
    }
  }

  bind_rows(lapply(rows, function(r) as_tibble(as.list(r))))
}

t1 <- table1(
  df,
  stratify_col     = "readmitted_30",
  continuous_cols  = c("age", "los_days", "total_charge"),
  categorical_cols = c("sex", "payer", "admit_type", "age_group")
)

7. Statistical Tests for Group Comparisons

cat("Statistical tests: readmitted vs not readmitted\n\n")

# --- Continuous: LOS (skewed → Mann-Whitney U) ---
g0 <- df$los_days[df$readmitted_30 == 0]
g1 <- df$los_days[df$readmitted_30 == 1]
mw <- wilcox.test(g0, g1, alternative = "two.sided", exact = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("LOS — Mann-Whitney U: U=%.0f, p=%.4f\n", mw$statistic, mw$p.value))

LOS — Mann-Whitney U: U=13498, p=0.2142

# --- Continuous: Age (normal → t-test) ---
g0a <- df$age[df$readmitted_30 == 0]
g1a <- df$age[df$readmitted_30 == 1]
tt  <- t.test(g0a, g1a, var.equal = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Age — Student t-test: t=%.3f, p=%.4f\n", tt$statistic, tt$p.value))

2. Synthetic Hospital Discharge Dataset

set.seed(42)
N <- 800

ages      <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes     <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers    <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                    N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
drg_codes <- sample(c(470, 291, 392, 690, 871, 193, 247, 603), N, replace = TRUE)
drg_labels_map <- c(
  `470` = "Major joint replacement", `291` = "Heart failure & shock",
  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)
los_days   <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges    <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
charges[runif(N) < 0.08] <- NA_real_
primary_dx <- sample(c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "I50.9", "J18.9", "A41.9", "M16.11", "N39.0"),
                     N, replace = TRUE)
admit_type <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
                     N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02))
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  drg_code      = drg_codes,
  drg_label     = unname(drg_labels_map[as.character(drg_codes)]),
  primary_dx    = primary_dx,
  admit_type    = admit_type,
  los_days      = los_days,
  total_charge  = charges,
  diabetes      = rbinom(N, 1, 0.32),
  hypertension  = rbinom(N, 1, 0.45),
  ckd           = rbinom(N, 1, 0.15),
  heart_failure = rbinom(N, 1, 0.18),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14)
)
bins <- c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95)
df$age_group <- cut(df$age, breaks = bins, labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"))

start <- as.Date("2019-01-01")
set.seed(5)
n_days <- as.integer(as.Date("2023-12-31") - start)
df$admit_date     <- start + sample(0:(n_days - 1), N, replace = TRUE)
df$discharge_date <- df$admit_date + df$los_days
df <- df %>% arrange(admit_date)

text:
6. Interpreting the Profile Report
The report is divided into five sections. Here is what to look for in each.







Section
What to check




Overview
Number of variables, rows, missing cells, duplicate rows


Variables
Distribution shape, % missing, distinct count, warnings (high cardinality, skewed, zeros)


Interactions
Bivariate scatter plots — look for clusters or non-linear relationships


Correlations
Pearson (linear), Spearman (monotonic) — flag high correlations (>0.8)


Missing values
Bar chart + matrix — check if missingness clusters on specific patients or time periods


Sample
First/last rows — sanity check on values and date formatting




# --- Extract key stats programmatically from the profile object ---
intro <- introduce(df)

cat("=== Profile Overview ===\n")

=== Profile Overview ===

cat(sprintf("  Dataset: %d rows, %d variables\n", intro$rows, intro$columns))

  Dataset: 800 rows, 18 variables

cat(sprintf("  Missing cells: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            intro$total_missing_values, 100 * intro$total_missing_values / intro$total_observations))

  Missing cells: 67 (0.5%)

cat(sprintf("  Duplicate rows: %d\n", sum(duplicated(df))))

  Duplicate rows: 0

cat("\n=== Variable-level warnings ===\n")


=== Variable-level warnings ===

n <- nrow(df)
for (col in names(df)) {
  x <- df[[col]]
  n_miss <- sum(is.na(x))
  n_uniq <- n_distinct(x)
  alerts <- character(0)
  if (n_uniq == n) alerts <- c(alerts, "HIGH CARDINALITY")
  if (n_miss / n > 0.05) alerts <- c(alerts, "MISSING")
  if (is.numeric(x) && sum(x == 0, na.rm = TRUE) / n > 0.20) alerts <- c(alerts, "ZEROS")
  if (is.numeric(x) && sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    sk <- mean((x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))^3, na.rm = TRUE) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)^3
    if (abs(sk) > 1) alerts <- c(alerts, "SKEWED")
  }
  if (length(alerts)) {
    for (a in alerts) cat(sprintf("  [%-20s] %s\n", a, col))
  }
}

title: Visualising Clinical Distributions
text:
1. Setup

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ggridges)
library(scales)

mod02_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod02")
dir.create(mod02_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

theme_health <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_health())

skewness <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  if (n < 3 || s == 0) return(NA_real_)
  mean((x - m)^3) / (s^3)
}

# ── Dataset ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 800
ages      <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes     <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers    <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                    N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
drg_codes <- sample(c(470, 291, 392, 690, 871, 193, 247, 603), N, replace = TRUE)
drg_labels_map <- c(
  `470` = "Major joint replacement", `291` = "Heart failure & shock",
  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)
los_days   <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges    <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
charges[runif(N) < 0.08] <- NA_real_
primary_dx <- sample(c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "I50.9", "J18.9", "A41.9", "M16.11", "N39.0"),
                     N, replace = TRUE)
admit_type <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
                     N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02))
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  drg_code      = drg_codes,
  drg_label     = unname(drg_labels_map[as.character(drg_codes)]),
  primary_dx    = primary_dx,
  admit_type    = admit_type,
  los_days      = los_days,
  total_charge  = charges,
  diabetes      = rbinom(N, 1, 0.32),
  hypertension  = rbinom(N, 1, 0.45),
  ckd           = rbinom(N, 1, 0.15),
  heart_failure = rbinom(N, 1, 0.18),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14)
)
df$age_group <- cut(df$age, breaks = c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95),
                    labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"))

# Synthetic lab values
set.seed(21)
df$glucose    <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 105, 28), 50), 400), 1)
df$creatinine <- round(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 1.6, scale = 0.6), 0.4), 10), 2)
df$hba1c      <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 6.8, 1.4), 4), 14), 1)
df$wbc        <- round(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 4, scale = 2), 1), 30), 1)
df$hemoglobin <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 12.8, 2.1), 5), 18), 1)

cat(sprintf("Dataset ready: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))

# ── Base dataset ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sexes    <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers   <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
                   N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03))
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges  <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
set.seed(99)
df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = payers,
  los_days      = los_days,
  diabetes      = rbinom(N, 1, 0.32),
  hypertension  = rbinom(N, 1, 0.45),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14),
  total_charge  = charges
)

# ── Introduce structured missingness (realistic clinical patterns) ─────────────
set.seed(7)

# MCAR — completely random (8% glucose)
df$glucose <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 105, 28), 50), 400), 1)
df$glucose[runif(N) < 0.08] <- NA_real_

# MAR — missing more often in Self-pay (lab deferral due to cost)
df$creatinine <- round(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 1.6, scale = 0.6), 0.4), 10), 2)
selfpay_mask <- df$payer == "Self-pay"
df$creatinine[selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.55)] <- NA_real_
df$creatinine[!selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.10)] <- NA_real_

# MNAR — HbA1c missing more often when values are in normal range (not ordered)
df$hba1c <- round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 6.8, 1.4), 4), 14), 1)
low_hba1c <- df$hba1c < 5.7
df$hba1c[low_hba1c & (runif(N) < 0.60)] <- NA_real_
df$hba1c[!low_hba1c & (runif(N) < 0.15)] <- NA_real_

# Charge missing correlated with Self-pay
df$total_charge <- charges
df$total_charge[selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.40)] <- NA_real_
df$total_charge[!selfpay_mask & (runif(N) < 0.05)] <- NA_real_

4. Imputation Strategies

# Store complete-case subsets for comparison
glucose_complete <- df$glucose[!is.na(df$glucose)]

# ── 4.1  Median imputation (simple, robust to outliers) ─────────────────────
df$glucose_median <- naniar::impute_median(df$glucose)
cat(sprintf("Median imputed: %d NaN → 0\n", sum(is.na(df$glucose))))

Median imputed: 74 NaN → 0

# ── 4.2  LOCF — Last Observation Carried Forward (longitudinal data) ─────────
# Simulate a longitudinal HbA1c series for 50 patients over 4 quarters
set.seed(55)
n_pts <- 50
n_periods <- 4
long_df <- tibble(
  patient_id = rep(sprintf("PT-%03d", seq_len(n_pts)), each = n_periods),
  quarter    = rep(seq_len(n_periods) - 1L, times = n_pts),
  hba1c      = round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pts * n_periods, 6.8, 1.2), 4), 13), 1)
)
# Introduce 25% missingness
long_df$hba1c[runif(nrow(long_df)) < 0.25] <- NA_real_
long_df <- long_df %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  arrange(quarter, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  fill(hba1c, .direction = "down") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(hba1c_locf = hba1c)
n_still_missing <- sum(is.na(long_df$hba1c_locf))
cat(sprintf("\nLOCF — residual missing after forward fill: %d\n", n_still_missing))


LOCF — residual missing after forward fill: 24

cat("(Residual = rows where patient has no prior observation)\n")

(Residual = rows where patient has no prior observation)



# ── 4.3  KNN Imputation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
num_cols <- c("age", "los_days", "glucose", "creatinine", "hba1c", "total_charge")
df_num   <- df %>% select(all_of(num_cols))

knn_impute <- function(dat, k = 5) {
  x <- as.matrix(dat)
  mus <- apply(x, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  sds <- apply(x, 2, sd,   na.rm = TRUE)
  sds[sds == 0 | is.na(sds)] <- 1
  xs <- sweep(sweep(x, 2, mus, "-"), 2, sds, "/")
  xs_fill <- xs
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(xs_fill))) {
    xs_fill[is.na(xs_fill[, j]), j] <- 0
  }
  miss <- which(is.na(x), arr.ind = TRUE)
  out <- x
  for (i in unique(miss[, 1])) {
    cols_miss <- miss[miss[, 1] == i, 2, drop = TRUE]
    d <- sqrt(rowSums((xs_fill -
                         matrix(xs_fill[i, ], nrow = nrow(xs_fill),
                                ncol = ncol(xs_fill), byrow = TRUE))^2))
    d[i] <- Inf
    nn <- order(d)[seq_len(min(k, length(d) - 1))]
    w  <- 1 / pmax(d[nn], 1e-8)
    w  <- w / sum(w)
    for (j in cols_miss) {
      out[i, j] <- sum(w * (xs_fill[nn, j] * sds[j] + mus[j]))
    }
  }
  as.data.frame(out)
}

mice_imp <- mice(
  df_num,
  m      = 5,
  maxit  = 10,
  method = "pmm",
  seed   = 42,

2. Synthetic Geospatial Dataset — 50 ZIP Code Areas

set.seed(42)

# ── Simulate 50 ZIP code areas (modelled on a mid-size US metropolitan area) ──
N_ZIPS <- 50

# Geographic centroids (roughly spanning a metro area, lat/lon)
lat_center <- 43.0
lon_center <- -76.1   # ~ Upstate NY
zip_df <- tibble(
  zip           = sprintf("%05d", 10000 + seq_len(N_ZIPS) - 1),
  tract_name    = sprintf("Tract %d", 100 + seq_len(N_ZIPS) - 1),
  lat           = runif(N_ZIPS, lat_center - 0.5, lat_center + 0.5),
  lon           = runif(N_ZIPS, lon_center - 0.5, lon_center + 0.5),
  population    = sample(3000:25000, N_ZIPS, replace = TRUE),
  pct_poverty   = rbeta(N_ZIPS, 2, 8) * 50,     # 0-50%
  pct_uninsured = rbeta(N_ZIPS, 1.5, 8) * 30,
  median_income = pmin(pmax(rnorm(N_ZIPS, 52000, 18000), 15000), 120000),
  svi_score     = rbeta(N_ZIPS, 2, 3),          # CDC SVI 0–1, higher=worse
  pct_elderly   = rbeta(N_ZIPS, 2, 6) * 40,     # % aged 65+
  urban_rural   = sample(c("Urban", "Suburban", "Rural"), N_ZIPS,
                         replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.50, 0.35, 0.15))
)

# Hospitalisations inversely correlated with income and SVI
zip_df$hosp_rate <- pmin(pmax(
  200
  + zip_df$svi_score * 180
  - zip_df$median_income / 1000 * 1.5
  + zip_df$pct_elderly * 4.5
  + rnorm(N_ZIPS, 0, 25),
  50), 600)

# Readmission rate
zip_df$readmit_rate <- pmin(pmax(
  12
  + zip_df$svi_score * 10
  + zip_df$pct_poverty * 0.18
  + rnorm(N_ZIPS, 0, 1.5),
  5), 35)

# Age-adjusted rate (add noise to crude to simulate adjustment)
zip_df$hosp_rate_adj <- pmin(pmax(
  zip_df$hosp_rate - zip_df$pct_elderly * 3.2 + rnorm(N_ZIPS, 0, 15),
  50), 600)

cat(sprintf("ZIP code dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(zip_df), ncol(zip_df)))

3. Patient-to-ZIP Assignment & Aggregation

# ── Generate patient discharge records with ZIP codes ─────────────────────────
set.seed(99)
N <- 800
# Assign patients to ZIPs weighted by population

patient_zips <- sample(zip_df$zip, size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = zip_weights)

patients <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  zip           = patient_zips,
  age           = as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95)),
  sex           = sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52)),
  los_days      = as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30)),
  readmitted_30 = rbinom(N, 1, 0.14),
  total_charge  = round(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30) * 2500, 2)
)

# Aggregate to ZIP level
zip_agg <- patients %>%
  group_by(zip) %>%
  summarise(
    n_discharges = n(),
    n_readmitted = sum(readmitted_30),
    mean_los     = mean(los_days),
    mean_charge  = mean(total_charge),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(observed_readmit_rate = n_readmitted / n_discharges * 100)

# Merge with ZIP reference table
zip_merged <- zip_df %>%
  left_join(zip_agg, by = "zip") %>%
  mutate(
    n_discharges = replace_na(n_discharges, 0),
    n_readmitted = replace_na(n_readmitted, 0)
  )

title: Hypothesis Testing for Health Outcomes
text:
2. Test Selection Framework
Outcome type?
├── Categorical (proportions) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
│     ├── 2 groups, expected counts ≥5 → Chi-square test
│     ├── 2 groups, small N or sparse cells → Fisher's exact test
│     └── >2 groups → Chi-square (or log-linear model)
│
├── Continuous, 2 groups ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│     ├── Check normality (Shapiro-Wilk n<50, D'Agostino n≥50)
│     │     ├── Normal + equal variance → Independent samples t-test
│     │     ├── Normal + unequal variance → Welch's t-test
│     │     └── Non-normal (LOS, charges) → Mann-Whitney U
│     └── Paired / matched → Paired t-test (normal) or Wilcoxon signed-rank
│
├── Continuous, >2 groups ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│     ├── Normal + equal variance → One-way ANOVA + post-hoc Tukey HSD
│     └── Non-normal → Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn's test
│
└── Count / rate outcome → Poisson test or negative binomial

3. Normality Assessment

# D'Agostino-Pearson analogue: moments test via Pearson's chi-square of skew + kurtosis
dagostino_pearson <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m3 <- mean((x - mean(x))^3)
  m4 <- mean((x - mean(x))^4)
  s  <- sd(x)
  skew <- m3 / s^3
  kurt <- m4 / s^4 - 3
  z_skew <- skew / sqrt(6 / n)
  z_kurt <- kurt / sqrt(24 / n)
  stat <- z_skew^2 + z_kurt^2
  p <- pchisq(stat, df = 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
  list(statistic = stat, p.value = p)
}

normality_report <- function(series, name) {
  s <- series[!is.na(series)]
  skewness <- mean((s - mean(s))^3) / sd(s)^3
  if (length(s) < 50) {
    sw <- shapiro.test(s)
    stat <- unname(sw$statistic)
    p <- sw$p.value
    test_name <- "Shapiro-Wilk"
  } else {
    dp <- dagostino_pearson(s)
    stat <- dp$statistic
    p <- dp$p.value
    test_name <- "D'Agostino"
  }
  normal <- p > 0.05
  cat(sprintf(
    "  %-20s: skew=%+.2f | %s p=%.4f → %s\n",
    name, skewness, test_name, p,
    if (normal) "NORMAL" else "NON-NORMAL"
  ))
  normal
}

# ── 4.3  Relative Risk and Odds Ratio ─────────────────────────────────────────
rr_or_correct <- function(exposed, outcome, label = "") {
  a <- sum(exposed == 1 & outcome == 1)
  b <- sum(exposed == 1 & outcome == 0)
  c <- sum(exposed == 0 & outcome == 1)
  d <- sum(exposed == 0 & outcome == 0)
  n_exp <- a + b; n_unexp <- c + d
  risk_e <- a / n_exp; risk_u <- c / n_unexp
  RR <- risk_e / risk_u
  OR <- if (b * c > 0) (a * d) / (b * c) else NA_real_
  se_log_rr <- sqrt((1 - risk_e) / a + (1 - risk_u) / c)
  se_log_or <- sqrt(1 / a + 1 / b + 1 / c + 1 / d)
  rr_lo <- exp(log(RR) - 1.96 * se_log_rr)
  rr_hi <- exp(log(RR) + 1.96 * se_log_rr)
  or_lo <- exp(log(OR) - 1.96 * se_log_or)
  or_hi <- exp(log(OR) + 1.96 * se_log_or)
  cat(sprintf("\n%s\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  RR = %.2f (95%% CI: %.2f–%.2f)\n", RR, rr_lo, rr_hi))
  cat(sprintf("  OR = %.2f (95%% CI: %.2f–%.2f)\n", OR, or_lo, or_hi))
}

# Brown-Forsythe (median-centred Levene) for equal variance
levene_bf <- function(x, g) {
  med <- tapply(x, g, median)
  z <- abs(x - med[as.character(g)])
  summary(aov(z ~ factor(g)))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1]
}

8. Statistical vs Clinical Significance

# Power analysis: what N is needed to detect a clinically meaningful difference?
# Two-sided two-sample t-test power (equal n, equal variance)
t_power <- function(d, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  nu  <- 2 * n - 2
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n / 2)
  crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, nu)
  pt(-crit, nu, ncp = ncp) + (1 - pt(crit, nu, ncp = ncp))
}

solve_n_power <- function(d, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80) {
  n <- 10
  while (t_power(d, n, alpha) < power && n < 1e5) n <- n + 1
  n
}

# Scenario: detecting a 1-day mean difference in LOS (SD ≈ 3.5 days)
effect_d <- 1.0 / 3.5   # Cohen's d for 1-day difference
n_needed <- solve_n_power(effect_d, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80)
cat("To detect a 1-day mean LOS difference (SD=3.5 days):\n")

To detect a 1-day mean LOS difference (SD=3.5 days):

  list(d = 0.5, label = "d=0.5 (medium)", color = "#2563EB"),
  list(d = 0.8, label = "d=0.8 (large)",  color = "#1E3A8A")
), function(spec) {
  tibble(n = ns, power = vapply(ns, function(n) t_power(spec$d, n), numeric(1)),
         label = spec$label, color = spec$color)
}))

p_a <- ggplot(power_df, aes(n, power, colour = label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, colour = "#DC2626", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(

               "d=0.8 (large)" = "#1E3A8A")

  mutate(sig = p < 0.05, n = factor(n, levels = as.character(ns_sim)))

  geom_col() +

text:
9. Knowledge Check

Why should you use Mann-Whitney U instead of t-test for LOS comparisons in most health datasets?
An OR of 2.1 (95% CI: 1.9–2.3) for diabetes → readmission is statistically significant. Is it clinically meaningful? What else do you need to know?
You run 20 chi-square tests comparing comorbidities. How many would you expect to be significant at α=0.05 by chance alone?
Bonferroni vs BH FDR: when is each preferred in health research?
You find p=0.001 for a 0.3-day LOS difference with N=5,000. Should you change clinical practice?

1. Setup & Survival Dataset

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod03_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod03")
dir.create(mod03_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

# ── Synthetic survival dataset: time to 30-day readmission ───────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 1500
base <- matrix(rnorm(N * 3), ncol = 3)

set.seed(99)
diabetes      <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.6 * base[, 1] - 0.5))
heart_failure <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * base[, 2] - 1.2))
copd          <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 3] - 1.0))
payers        <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.42, 0.22, 0.28, 0.08)
)
ages     <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes    <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))

# Time to readmission (days after discharge, max follow-up = 365)
# Shorter time for patients with HF, diabetes, high LOS
hazard <- exp(-3.5 + 0.5 * heart_failure + 0.3 * diabetes + 0.15 * (los_days > 7) + 0.2 * copd)
time_to_event <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rexp(N, rate = hazard), 1), 365))

# Censoring: some patients lost to follow-up before 365 days (30% censored)
censor_time <- as.integer(round(runif(N, 30, 365)))
observed    <- as.integer(time_to_event <= censor_time)   # 1 = event observed
duration    <- ifelse(observed == 1, time_to_event, censor_time)

df <- tibble(
  patient_id      = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age             = ages,
  sex             = sexes,
  payer           = payers,
  los_days        = los_days,
  diabetes        = diabetes,
  heart_failure   = heart_failure,
  copd            = copd,
  duration_days   = duration,
  event_observed  = observed
) |>
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(age, breaks = c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95),
                    labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+")),
    high_risk = as.integer(heart_failure == 1 | diabetes == 1)
  )

cat(sprintf("Survival dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))

Survival dataset: 1500 x 12

cat(sprintf("Event rate (readmission observed): %.1f%%\n", mean(df$event_observed) * 100))

Event rate (readmission observed): 98.3%

cat(sprintf("Censoring rate               : %.1f%%\n", (1 - mean(df$event_observed)) * 100))

2. The Censoring Concept

Censoring occurs when the event has not yet happened by the end of follow-up, or when a patient is lost. The censored observation still contributes information: we know the patient was event-free up to their last contact.









Censoring type
Meaning
Example




Right-censored
Event not yet occurred at study end
Patient still alive at end of follow-up


Left-censored
Event occurred before first observation
Readmission before first clinic visit


Interval-censored
Event occurred between two observations
Only know readmission was between visits



In most clinical registry analyses, right-censoring is the norm.

# Restricted mean survival time (RMST) up to t* = 180 days
rmst_from_survfit <- function(fit, t_max = 180) {
  sm <- summary(fit, times = seq(0, t_max, by = 1), extend = TRUE)
  times <- sm$time
  surv  <- sm$surv
  if (min(times) > 0) {
    times <- c(0, times)
    surv  <- c(1, surv)
  }
  if (max(times) < t_max) {
    times <- c(times, t_max)
    surv  <- c(surv, tail(surv, 1))
  }
  sum(diff(times) * head(surv, -1))
}

7. Interpreting Crossing Survival Curves

# Simulate crossing curves — when log-rank may be misleading
set.seed(33)
n_cross <- 500
# Group A: early-risk high, late-risk low
t_A <- pmin(pmax(rexp(n_cross, rate = 1 / 60), 1), 365)
e_A <- rbinom(n_cross, 1, 0.65)
# Group B: early-risk low, late-risk high (crossing pattern)
t_B <- c(
  pmin(pmax(rexp(n_cross / 2, rate = 1 / 200), 1), 180),
  pmin(pmax(rexp(n_cross / 2, rate = 1 / 40), 181), 365)
)
e_B <- rbinom(n_cross, 1, 0.60)

cross_df <- tibble(
  time  = c(t_A, t_B),
  event = c(e_A, e_B),
  group = factor(rep(c("Group A (early risk)", "Group B (late risk)"), each = n_cross))
)
km_cross <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ group, data = cross_df)
lr_cross <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ group, data = cross_df)
# Wilcoxon (Breslow / Gehan) weighted log-rank — more power for early differences
wilcox_cross <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ group, data = cross_df, rho = 1)
p_lr <- 1 - pchisq(lr_cross$chisq, 1)
p_w  <- 1 - pchisq(wilcox_cross$chisq, 1)

p_cross <- ggsurvplot(
  km_cross, data = cross_df, conf.int = TRUE,
  palette = c("#DC2626", "#2563EB"),
  xlab = "Days", ylab = "S(t)",
  title = "Crossing survival curves — log-rank test loses power\nConsider Wilcoxon (Breslow) test or weighted log-rank",
  legend.title = "", ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
p_cross$plot <- p_cross$plot +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = 0.18, hjust = 1.05, size = 3.2,
           label = sprintf("Log-rank p = %.4f\nWilcoxon p = %.4f\n(may miss crossing)", p_lr, p_w)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05))

A patient who withdraws from the study on day 45 without experiencing the event — how should they be coded (duration, event_observed)?

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod03_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod03")
dir.create(mod03_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

set.seed(42)
N <- 2000
base <- matrix(rnorm(N * 3), ncol = 3)

set.seed(99)
ages          <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes         <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers        <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03)
)
diabetes      <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.6 * base[, 1] - 0.5))
heart_failure <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * base[, 2] - 1.2))
copd          <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 3] - 1.0))
hypertension  <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.7 * base[, 1] - 0.2))
los_days      <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
admit_type    <- sample(c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent"), N, replace = TRUE,
                        prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.18))
n_comorb      <- diabetes + heart_failure + copd + hypertension

readmit_logit <- (-3.0 + 0.7 * heart_failure + 0.5 * diabetes + 0.4 * copd
                  + 0.02 * (ages - 60) + 0.3 * as.integer(admit_type == "Emergency")
                  + 0.2 * as.integer(los_days > 7) + 0.3 * as.integer(payers == "Medicaid")
                  + rnorm(N, 0, 0.3))
readmitted_30 <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(readmit_logit))

df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = ages,
  sex           = sexes,
  payer         = relevel(factor(payers), ref = "Private"),
  admit_type    = relevel(factor(admit_type), ref = "Elective"),
  los_days      = los_days,
  los_gt7       = as.integer(los_days > 7),
  diabetes      = diabetes,
  heart_failure = heart_failure,
  copd          = copd,
  hypertension  = hypertension,
  n_comorb      = n_comorb,
  readmitted_30 = readmitted_30
) |>
  mutate(age_std = as.numeric(scale(age)))

cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))

Dataset: 2000 x 14

4. Multicollinearity — Variance Inflation Factor

# VIF for continuous and binary predictors
vif_from_lm <- function(data, vars) {
  X <- data[, vars, drop = FALSE]
  vapply(vars, function(v) {
    others <- setdiff(vars, v)
    r2 <- summary(lm(as.formula(paste(v, "~", paste(others, collapse = "+"))),
                     data = X))$r.squared
    1 / (1 - r2)
  }, numeric(1))
}

6. Hosmer-Lemeshow Goodness-of-Fit

hosmer_lemeshow <- function(y_true, y_pred, n_groups = 10) {
  # Hosmer-Lemeshow test for logistic regression calibration.
  df_hl <- tibble(y = y_true, p = y_pred) |>
    mutate(decile = ntile(p, n_groups))
  grouped <- df_hl |>
    group_by(decile) |>
    summarise(
      obs_pos = sum(y),
      obs_neg = sum(y == 0),
      exp_pos = sum(p),
      exp_neg = sum(1 - p),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  hl_stat <- sum((grouped$obs_pos - grouped$exp_pos)^2 / grouped$exp_pos +
                   (grouped$obs_neg - grouped$exp_neg)^2 / grouped$exp_neg)
  p_val <- 1 - pchisq(hl_stat, df = n_groups - 2)
  list(stat = hl_stat, p = p_val)
}

1. Setup & Dataset

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)
library(dagitty)
library(ggdag)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod03_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod03")
dir.create(mod03_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

set.seed(42)
N <- 3000

# ── Age is a confounder: older → more diabetes AND more readmission ────────────
age <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 15), 18), 95))
age_std <- (age - 62) / 15

diabetes <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(-1.0 + 0.05 * age_std))
sex      <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payer    <- sample(c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private"), N, replace = TRUE,
                   prob = c(0.42, 0.22, 0.36))
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
hf       <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(-1.8 + 0.6 * diabetes + 0.04 * age_std))

# Readmission: diabetes → readmission but age is a confounder
readmit_logit <- (-2.8 + 0.5 * diabetes + 0.03 * age_std + 0.6 * hf
                  + 0.2 * as.integer(payer == "Medicaid")
                  + 0.15 * as.integer(los_days > 7)
                  + rnorm(N, 0, 0.2))
readmitted <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(readmit_logit))

# Effect modifier: diabetes effect on readmission is STRONGER in patients with HF
readmit_em_logit <- (-2.8 + 0.3 * diabetes + 0.03 * age_std + 0.6 * hf
                     + 0.9 * diabetes * hf              # interaction term
                     + 0.2 * as.integer(payer == "Medicaid")
                     + rnorm(N, 0, 0.2))
readmitted_em <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(readmit_em_logit))

df <- tibble(
  patient_id    = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age           = age,
  age_std       = age_std,
  sex           = sex,
  payer         = relevel(factor(payer), ref = "Private"),
  los_days      = los_days,
  diabetes      = diabetes,
  hf            = hf,
  readmitted    = readmitted,
  readmitted_em = readmitted_em
) |>
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(age, breaks = c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95),
                    labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+"))
  )

cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))

Dataset: 3000 x 11

cat(sprintf("Diabetes prevalence   : %.1f%%\n", mean(diabetes) * 100))

Diabetes prevalence   : 25.9%

cat(sprintf("Readmission prevalence: %.1f%%\n", mean(readmitted) * 100))

Readmission prevalence: 8.4%

title: Confounding & Effect Modification
text:
2. What is Confounding?
A confounder is a variable that is associated with both the exposure and the outcome, but is not on the causal pathway between them.
        Age
       ↙    ↘
Diabetes → Readmission
Age → more diabetes (older patients have more diabetes)
Age → more readmission (older patients readmit more)
Age is NOT caused by diabetes
Effect: crude OR for diabetes → readmission is inflated because age is “lurking” in the background.

# ── Demonstrate confounding: crude vs adjusted estimate ──────────────────────
crude_or <- function(exposed, outcome) {
  a <- sum(exposed == 1 & outcome == 1)
  b <- sum(exposed == 1 & outcome == 0)
  c <- sum(exposed == 0 & outcome == 1)
  d <- sum(exposed == 0 & outcome == 0)
  OR <- if (b * c > 0) (a * d) / (b * c) else NA_real_
  se <- sqrt(1 / a + 1 / b + 1 / c + 1 / d)
  c(OR, exp(log(OR) - 1.96 * se), exp(log(OR) + 1.96 * se))
}

# Crude
cr <- crude_or(df$diabetes, df$readmitted)

# Adjusted (logistic regression)
model_adj <- glm(
  readmitted ~ diabetes + age_std + sex + payer + hf + los_days,
  data = df, family = binomial()
)
tid_dm <- broom::tidy(model_adj, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  filter(term == "diabetes")
adj_or_val <- tid_dm$estimate
adj_lo <- tid_dm$conf.low
adj_hi <- tid_dm$conf.high

cat("Diabetes → 30-day readmission\n")

Diabetes → 30-day readmission

cat(sprintf("  Crude OR (unadjusted): %.3f  (95%% CI: %.3f–%.3f)\n", cr[1], cr[2], cr[3]))

  Crude OR (unadjusted): 1.894  (95% CI: 1.449–2.475)

cat(sprintf("  Adjusted OR           : %.3f  (95%% CI: %.3f–%.3f)\n", adj_or_val, adj_lo, adj_hi))

  Adjusted OR           : 1.721  (95% CI: 1.305–2.259)

cat("\n")
pct_change <- (adj_or_val - cr[1]) / cr[1] * 100
cat(sprintf("  %% change after adjustment: %+.1f%%\n\n", pct_change))

  % change after adjustment: -9.1%

if (abs(pct_change) > 10) {
  cat("  ✗ Meaningful confounding detected (>10% change rule)\n")
} else {
  cat("  ✓ Little confounding (< 10% change)\n")
}

  ✓ Little confounding (< 10% change)

# Mantel-Haenszel stratified OR by age group
mh <- mantelhaen.test(xtabs(~ diabetes + readmitted + age_group, data = df))

4. Effect Modification (Interaction)

# Test whether HF MODIFIES the effect of diabetes on readmission
# (as opposed to HF merely being a confounder)

# Model without interaction
model_no_int <- glm(
  readmitted_em ~ diabetes + hf + age_std + payer,
  data = df, family = binomial()
)

# Model with interaction
model_int <- glm(
  readmitted_em ~ diabetes * hf + age_std + payer,
  data = df, family = binomial()
)

# Likelihood ratio test for interaction term
lr <- anova(model_no_int, model_int, test = "LRT")
lr_stat <- lr$Deviance[2]
lr_p    <- lr$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]

cat("Likelihood ratio test for diabetes × HF interaction:\n")

Likelihood ratio test for diabetes × HF interaction:

cat(sprintf("  LR statistic = %.3f, df=1, p = %.4f\n\n", lr_stat, lr_p))

  LR statistic = 18.258, df=1, p = 0.0000

if (!is.na(lr_p) && lr_p < 0.05) {
  cat("  ✓ Significant interaction — effect modification is present\n")
  cat("  → Report STRATUM-SPECIFIC effects, not a single pooled estimate\n")
} else {
  cat("  ✗ No significant interaction — no effect modification\n")
  cat("  → A single adjusted estimate is appropriate\n")
}

  ✓ Significant interaction — effect modification is present
  → Report STRATUM-SPECIFIC effects, not a single pooled estimate

# Stratum-specific ORs
cat("\nStratum-specific OR for diabetes → readmission:\n")


Stratum-specific OR for diabetes → readmission:

for (pair in list(list(0, "No HF"), list(1, "HF present"))) {
  hf_val <- pair[[1]]; label <- pair[[2]]
  sub <- df |> filter(hf == hf_val)
  a <- sum(sub$diabetes == 1 & sub$readmitted_em == 1)
  b <- sum(sub$diabetes == 1 & sub$readmitted_em == 0)
  c <- sum(sub$diabetes == 0 & sub$readmitted_em == 1)
  d <- sum(sub$diabetes == 0 & sub$readmitted_em == 0)
  or_s <- if (b * c > 0) (a * d) / (b * c) else NA_real_
  se   <- sqrt(1 / a + 1 / b + 1 / c + 1 / d)
  lo <- exp(log(or_s) - 1.96 * se)
  hi <- exp(log(or_s) + 1.96 * se)
  cat(sprintf("  %-15s: OR = %.2f  (95%% CI: %.2f–%.2f)\n", label, or_s, lo, hi))
}

  No HF          : OR = 1.17  (95% CI: 0.82–1.68)
  HF present     : OR = 4.18  (95% CI: 2.60–6.72)



# Visualise effect modification
strat_rates <- df |>
  group_by(hf, diabetes) |>
  summarise(rate = mean(readmitted_em) * 100, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    hf_lab = if_else(hf == 1, "HF", "No HF"),
    dm_lab = if_else(diabetes == 1, "Diabetes", "No diabetes")
